currentState: Chapter 7: a first working bond across a single afternoon. Corin hoped she was sent from the Citadel about his shipments; she says nobody sent her; she then asks the questions no one in Dalaran did (who he wrote to; did anyone answer) and takes up his paper. He becomes her hands and eyes for the written word (she cannot write; blots) and her access (the ring); she becomes the one who proves his copied marks true by reading the bags. He hugs the satchel and walks on her dead side.
powerDynamic: Jaina's rank and reputation (Lady Proudmoore of Dalaran) set her above him; she does not use it. She treats him as a colleague: 'Corin.', asks him questions, trusts his lists, dictates to him. He is deferential in word and independent in fact.

physicalDynamics.pattern: Corin pulls the stool out so fast it tips, catches it; presses an inky hand against the satchel after her 'Nobody sent me'; walks at her pace, the satchel in both arms, one hand a finger's width from her sleeve on her dead side; writes her readings at her dictation after her blots (the top sheet carries three lines of blots).

history.event: Chapter 7: Corin: 'Were you sent? About the shipments?' Jaina: 'No. Nobody sent me.' He keeps his hand on the satchel.
Chapter 7: Jaina asks who he wrote to; he lists the Citadel inspection desk and the Archmage's secretary; 'Did anyone answer?' 'No.' Her fingertips go white on the staff.

Chapter 7: sample room, offstage: she reads every shelf against his bills; he writes her answers. 'I tried. Then I talked, and he wrote.' He wanted her to stop at the first shelf; Sylvanas cuts him off ('Leave it.').

trajectory: Ch7: from stranger to working partner. Corin has a reason to trust her (she is the first Dalaran mage to listen); she has an ally who carries the paper.
